question: What was the purpose of Operation Brahma launched by India in March 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Earthquake relief**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation Brahma** was launched by **India in March 2025** as a dedicated mission aimed at providing **earthquake relief** in regions that were severely affected by a devastating earthquake.
 
• The operation was initiated in response to a **high-magnitude earthquake** that caused widespread destruction, including loss of life, damage to infrastructure, and displacement of populations.
 
• The primary objective of the operation was to provide **immediate humanitarian aid**, including rescue operations, medical assistance, and the distribution of food and essential supplies.
 
• The operation involved the collaboration of multiple agencies, including the **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)**, **Indian Armed Forces**, and various non-governmental organizations (NGOs).
 
• Specialized teams were deployed to conduct **search-and-rescue missions** using advanced equipment and trained personnel to locate and save individuals trapped under rubble.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Earthquakes in India:**

 
 
• India is highly vulnerable to earthquakes, with over **59% of its landmass** prone to seismic activity. The regions are classified into **four seismic zones (Zone II, III, IV, and V)**.
 
• Zone V is the most seismically active region, covering areas like **Northeast India, parts of Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat.**
 
• Major earthquakes in Indian history include the **Bihar-Nepal earthquake (1934)**, **Latur earthquake (1993)**, **Bhuj earthquake (2001)**, and the **Kashmir earthquake (2005).**
 
 
 
• **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF):**
 
 
• The **NDRF** is a specialized force established under the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**, for disaster response and management in India.
 
• It operates under the Ministry of Home Affairs and is trained for **rescue, relief, and rehabilitation operations** during natural and man-made disasters.
 
• The force is equipped with state-of-the-art rescue equipment, including seismic sensors, life detectors, and cutting tools.
 
 
 
• **Indian Armed Forces in Disaster Relief:**
 
 
• The **Indian Armed Forces** play a critical role in disaster management, especially in large-scale emergencies like earthquakes, floods, and cyclones.
 
• They provide logistics, transportation, and **airlift operations** to deliver aid to inaccessible areas.
 
• For example, during the **Bhuj earthquake (2001)**, the Indian Army and Air Force led massive relief and rescue operations in Gujarat.
 
 
 
• **Disaster Preparedness in India:**
 
 
• The **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** is the apex body responsible for formulating policies and guidelines for disaster management in India.
 
• India has also implemented early warning systems and conducts regular mock drills to enhance disaster preparedness.
 
• Community-based disaster risk reduction programs aim to educate and empower local populations to respond effectively during emergencies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Earthquake Magnitude:** The magnitude of an earthquake is measured on the **Richter scale**, which quantifies the energy released by the seismic event.
 
• **Seismic Building Codes:** India has introduced **seismic-resistant building codes** to ensure that infrastructure is designed to withstand earthquakes, especially in high-risk areas.
 
• **International Cooperation:** India collaborates with global organizations like the **United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR)** to enhance disaster resilience.
 
• **Key Initiatives:** Programs like the **Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015-2030)** guide India’s strategies for reducing disaster risks and enhancing preparedness.
